Title: Card Number Iframe Isolation
Preconditions:
[PRE:CLEAR_SESSION]
[PRE:SIGNIN_AS:USER_DEFAULT]
- CyberSource payment form displayed
- Browser DevTools open
Steps:
[NAV] {{FRONT_URL}}/cart - confirm the CyberSource card-payment form is displayed
[WAIT] the Card Number field finishes loading (CyberSource Flex Microform mounts into #cardNumber-container)
[KEY] inspect #cardNumber-container and record whether its rendered child is an <iframe> (per vc-frontend client-app/shared/payment/components/payment-processing-cyber-source.vue number.load(...)) or a plain <input> owned by the storefront page
[ACT] click into the Card Number iframe field and type @td(CYBERSOURCE_VISA.number)
[KEY] capture the storefront page own DOM/JS state after typing, excluding the iframe internal cross-origin document
Assertions:
[DOM] #cardNumber-container only rendered child is an <iframe> element - the field is not a same-origin <input> in the storefront page own DOM
[STATE] the typed card number does not appear anywhere in the storefront page own DOM outside the iframe (no attribute, hidden input or text node carries the digits)
[CONSOLE] no cross-origin/SecurityError is thrown when the SDK initializes or the page interacts with the container
Cross_Layer_Checks: [NETWORK] no request fired by the storefront page own JS (outside the iframe) carries the typed card number
Failure_Signals: Card Number field renders as a plain <input> in the storefront page own DOM (no iframe); the typed card number is readable from the parent page DOM or JS scope; console throws a cross-origin/SecurityError on field init
References: PCI-DSS SAQ A client-side field isolation. Grounded in vc-frontend client-app/shared/payment/components/payment-processing-cyber-source.vue (#cardNumber-container, number.load(...), CyberSource Flex Microform), source fetched live 2026-09-19. Business_Rule cleared: BL-SEC-00N does not exist (no BL-SEC-* family in the oracle) and no promoted invariant covers this behaviour - oracle gap, candidate for /qa-review-oracles.

[ACT] submit payment
[WAIT] the authorizePayment GraphQL response is received

Assertions:
[NETWORK] no request body, from any request the storefront page itself fires to {{BACK_URL}}, contains the raw card number or CVV
[BODY] the authorizePayment GraphQL mutation parameters array carries only the opaque token entry - no cardNumber/cvv/expiry field

[CONSOLE] no JS error logs the raw card data
Failure_Signals: Raw card number or CVV appears in any request body captured during the flow; authorizePayment parameters carry a raw card field instead of an opaque token

References: VCST-4576 (payment security family). [WAIT] Receive response

Title: Persistent Access Token — Revoked Token Returns 401 (State Transition: Active → Revoked)
Preconditions:
[PRE:CLEAR_SESSION]
- Admin credentials available
- Two contexts/tokens can be obtained independently
- The actual value of Authorization__EnablePersistentStorageTokenValidation is VERIFIED LIVE in Steps, never assumed
Steps:
[HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/settings?names=Authorization.EnablePersistentStorageTokenValidation and record PERSISTENT_VALIDATION_ENABLED
[HTTP] POST {{BACK_URL}}/connect/token credentials to obtain Token A (access_token + refresh_token)
[WAIT] Receive Token A
[HTTP] POST {{BACK_URL}}/connect/token again with same credentials to obtain Token B
[WAIT] Receive Token B (separate authorization entry)
[HTTP] POST {{BACK_URL}}/revoke/token with token=<Token A refresh_token>, token_type_hint=refresh_token, Authorization: Bearer <Token A access_token>
[WAIT] Revocation completes (HTTP 200)
[HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/security/users with Authorization: Bearer <Token A access_token>
[WAIT] Receive response
[HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/security/users with Authorization: Bearer <Token B access_token>
[WAIT] Receive response (expect 200)
Assertions:
[STATUS] POST /revoke/token returns HTTP 200
[STATUS] IF PERSISTENT_VALIDATION_ENABLED=true: GET /api/platform/security/users with revoked Token A returns HTTP 401; IF false: Token A remains valid until its documented TTL elapses - assert that TTL behaviour, NOT a 401
[BODY] the 401 response (when asserted) does not leak user data or internal paths
[STATUS] GET /api/platform/security/users with active Token B returns HTTP 200 (revocation is scoped to Token A only)
Cross_Layer_Checks:
[API] Token A rejected after revocation; Token B unaffected
[NETWORK] No 5xx errors on any request
Failure_Signals: POST /revoke/token returns non-200; PERSISTENT_VALIDATION_ENABLED=true but revoked Token A still authorizes (real defect); PERSISTENT_VALIDATION_ENABLED=false but Token A is rejected before its TTL elapses (real defect); Token B also rejected after Token A revocation (over-broad invalidation); 500 errors
Cleanup: Obtain new token and use to clean up any test state
References: VCST-4576; Corrected 2026-09-19 (REG-2026-09-19-1035): /connect/revocation does not exist - its 404 is a non-endpoint, not a defect - replaced with /revoke/token. The 401 check also moved off /currentuser, which is [Authorize]+[AllowAnonymous] and can never 401. The precondition required EnablePersistentStorageTokenValidation=true but never verified it; it is now read live and the assertion branches on it (platform default is false - see BUG_032_057, config-gated by design).

Title: Persistent Access Token — Never-Issued Token Returns 401
Preconditions:
[PRE:CLEAR_SESSION]
- Platform accessible
- Authorization__EnablePersistentStorageTokenValidation=true configured
Steps:
[HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/security/users with Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJmYWtlIn0.invalidsignature
[WAIT] Receive response (expect 401)
[HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/security/users with Authorization: Bearer AAAA.BBBB.CCCC
[WAIT] Receive response (expect 401)
[HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/security/currentuser with no Authorization header
[WAIT] Receive response (expect 200, anonymous-allowed by design)
Assertions:
[STATUS] Both /api/platform/security/users requests (fabricated and malformed tokens) return HTTP 401
[BODY] No user data in either 401 response
[BODY] No internal paths or stack traces in either error response
[STATUS] /api/platform/security/currentuser with no Authorization header returns HTTP 200 BY DESIGN ([Authorize]+[AllowAnonymous], vc-platform SecurityController.cs:259-263) - an anonymous-contract check, never a 401 expectation
[BODY] the anonymous 200 response body is empty and leaks no user data
Cross_Layer_Checks:
[API] No 500 returned for malformed tokens against /api/platform/security/users
[NETWORK] Both /users requests fail with 401, not 200
Failure_Signals: 200 returned by /api/platform/security/users for a fabricated/unsigned token; 500 Internal Server Error instead of 401; user data visible in error response body; the currentuser anonymous 200 response leaks user data (breaks the anonymous contract)
References: VCST-4576; Corrected 2026-09-19 (REG-2026-09-19-1035): the 401 assertions targeted /api/platform/security/currentuser, which is [Authorize]+[AllowAnonymous] in vc-platform source and therefore can NEVER return 401 for any input - an unfalsifiable oracle. Re-pointed at the permission-gated /users endpoint; the anonymous contract is now asserted separately.

Title: Session Invalidation After Password Change — Other Devices Logged Out
Preconditions:
[PRE:CLEAR_SESSION]
- Authorization__EnablePersistentStorageTokenValidation=true configured (enables OpenIddict DB-based revocation)
- User account available (use agent pool slot 1 for Device A context, slot 2 for Device B context)
- Two separate sessions can be established for the same user
Steps:
[HTTP] POST {{BACK_URL}}/connect/token for @td(ACME_BUYER.email) — obtain Token-A (Device A session)
[WAIT] Receive Token-A
[HTTP] POST {{BACK_URL}}/connect/token for @td(ACME_BUYER.email) again — obtain Token-B (Device B session)
[WAIT] Receive Token-B
[HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/security/currentuser with Token-A (Device B still active — verify pre-change)
[ASSERT] Both tokens return 200 before password change
[HTTP] POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/security/users/changepassword (or changePassword mutation via xAPI) using Token-A with currentPassword=@td(ACME_BUYER.password) and new password
[WAIT] Password change returns HTTP 200
[HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/security/currentuser with Token-B (Device B token — expect 401 after change)
[WAIT] Receive response
[HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/security/currentuser with Token-A (Device A token — should survive)
[WAIT] Receive response
Assertions:
[STATUS] Password change returns HTTP 200
[STATUS] Token-B returns HTTP 401 after password change (other-device session invalidated)
[BODY] Token-B 401 response contains no user data
[STATUS] Token-A continues to return HTTP 200 OR returns 401 (either is acceptable — behavior depends on platform implementation; the initiating-session-survives behavior is documented in VCST-4531 comment)
Cross_Layer_Checks:
[API] Token-B revoked after password change
[NETWORK] No 5xx errors
[ADMIN] Security > Users panel for the account shows no active authorizations for Token-B
Failure_Signals: Token-B still returns 200 after password change (invalidation not working); 500 errors on password change endpoint; Password change endpoint returns 4xx
Cleanup: Restore original password via admin API; clean up AGENT-TEST- sessions
